source.title: Learning is Forgetting: LLM Training As Lossy Compression
source.authors: Henry Conklin; Tom Hosking; Tan Yi-Chern; Julian Gold; Jonathan D. Cohen; Thomas L. Griffiths; Max Bartolo; Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant

record.tranche_reason: The study cites Kaplan et al.'s scaling-laws work but does not test or rely on the scaling-law claims. Its loss measurement is about training progress versus compression proximity, not loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.gate_note: The paper measures OLMo2 7B cross-entropy during pretraining, but does not fit or evaluate a power law or compare loss across parameter counts, token counts, or compute budgets. It also relates compression and preference-information measures—not scale or pretraining loss—to downstream scores. Those related results are recorded as versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study cites Kaplan et al. only to say its finding that smaller models compress less fits scaling-law work. It fits no power law and does not compare loss across parameters, tokens or compute. Its downstream correlations use information-plane measures, not scale or pretraining loss. So no version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also say smaller models (1B) fail to approach optimal compression, which they note is in line with Kaplan et al.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes representation information and compression; it does not apply the original scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that information-plane estimates vary somewhat with dataset and number of reference points, while retaining the described expansion/compression pattern. These sensitivities concern their compression estimates, not scaling-law fits.

fits_no_version.finding: OLMo2 7B C4 loss drops early in training and then slowly flattens as the model approaches the Information Bottleneck bound on compression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss saturation during pretraining coincides with the onset of representational compression.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 47 open-weights models, compression optimality (r=0.52) and preference information (r=0.76) correlate with aggregate benchmark scores, lower token complexity correlates with better scores (r=-0.38), and expressivity alone does not (r=0.08).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-plane measures of representations predict downstream benchmark performance.

record.problems: The loss plot gives no numerical checkpoint values or power-law fits, and its C4 evaluation is described as a proxy for in-distribution performance. The downstream results are correlations with different predictors from those named in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted. Other compression trajectories and performance correlations were not separately recorded where they do not add a distinct result relevant to the scaling-law claim.

untested.parts: No fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No comparison of model shapes at a fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits in other modalities or training regimes.

Downstream performance is related to compression and preference measures, not to scale or pretraining loss. Partial correlations controlling for parameter count are mentioned for Figure 6 but no values are given.
No exponents or fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: The only link to scaling laws is a qualitative observation about scale and compression, plus a citation of Kaplan et al. Neither is a test of loss scaling.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute, or whether other quantities are non-bottlenecks.
Does not fit scaling curves on small runs or compare their predictions with larger runs.
Does not find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations or test their trends with compute.
Does not compare architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Does not test the proposed power-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
Reports downstream correlations with compression and preference-information measures, not predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Does not test scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal fits, or departures from a fitted power law.

relation.reason: Section 4.1 cites Kaplan et al. when interpreting smaller models' failure to approach optimal compression; it does not test or apply the cited scaling law.

tranche.reason: The study measures representation compression and its downstream correlations. It neither tests nor uses V1–V7: no power-law loss fit, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture comparison, or downstream prediction from scale or pretraining loss.

source_check.notes: R5 matches Section 4.2 exactly, but the introduction reports p < 0.001 rather than p = 0.001. The scale comparison concerns compression optimality, and the downstream predictors are representation measures; neither tests the listed scaling-law versions.
